tasks.short: Draw this installation's piping and instrumentation diagrams.

steps.what: Walk this site and note the piping and instrumentation the system architecture must include.
inputs: this roof, plant room and pipe routes
the equipment the installation will use
outputs: notes of where piping and instrumentation must sit

steps.what: Develop the process flow diagram for that system architecture, including the piping and instrumentation.
inputs: notes of where piping and instrumentation must sit
outputs: the process flow diagram for this installation

steps.what: Maintain the diagrams when this installation's piping or instrumentation changes.
inputs: the process flow diagram for this installation

tasks.design: The installation manager still walks the site, still develops the process flow diagram, and still maintains it when the piping or instrumentation changes. No step is shorter. A copied symbol from an older diagram does not choose the routes on this roof or in this plant room, and no machine reads a roof photo. No survey record is produced for a later step to consume.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each installation's piping and instrumentation differ, and no standard drawing matches this site.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes that judgement. A symbol copied from an older diagram still has to be checked against this roof and this plant room.
tasks.still_hard: The routes, the instruments and the process flow are a judgement of this site. A wrong diagram is rework on the roof.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the real pipes, penetrations and plant room, and deciding the architecture that fits them.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The manager still spends this time on the site and at the diagram, and still decides the architecture.

reach.task: Open a wall or a roof the diagram did not show
reach.learn: To stop and ask the manager to revise the diagram before the route is built

evidence.claim: Laying out piping and instrumentation for one installation is a judgement of that site. A repeated symbol does not choose the routes, and a roof photo does not draw the diagram. Model knowledge.
Building installations must meet NEN 1010 (Bbl art. 4.199).
A photovoltaic system is part of that building installation, so the manager applies the same rule while drawing. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one installation's piping, instrumentation and process flow. The manager walks the site, draws the diagram and revises it when the installation changes. No step is shortened, so every remaining share stays at 100.
No survey record, equipment list or symbol library is produced for a machine. The diagram is drawn by the installation manager from what was seen. Nothing in this task reads a roof photo.

Building installations must meet NEN 1010 under Bbl art. 4.199. The manager applies that while drawing. It does not generate the diagram. Model knowledge adds that a photovoltaic system is part of that installation.
unknowns: Whether this firm already keeps a symbol set the manager trusts for a repeated plant-room layout.
How often the diagram changes after the crew opens the roof.
research_questions: On the last ten installations, how many diagram hours were redrawing a repeated symbol, and how many were deciding routes the last diagram did not have?

incremental.description: No drawing tool is added, so the manager has no new upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The manager still walks the site, still develops the diagram, and still maintains it. No step is shortened, so no time is saved on an installation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge subcontractor quality, cost and reliability.

steps.what: Read each subcontractor bid for scope, price, exclusions and a validity date.
inputs: the subcontractor bids for this installation
outputs: what each bid covers, excludes and prices

steps.what: Type each subcontractor line as scope, quantity, unit price, exclusions and validity date so the sheet can multiply.
inputs: what each bid covers, excludes and prices
outputs: typed lines and the sheet's line totals

steps.what: Evaluate each subcontractor's quality and reliability for this installation.
inputs: what each bid covers, excludes and prices
outputs: the manager's judgement of quality and reliability

steps.what: Discuss the comparison with the bidder and leave the subcontractor choice with the manager.
inputs: typed lines and the sheet's line totals
the manager's judgement of quality and reliability
outputs: what was discussed, and the manager's choice

tasks.design: The only shorter step is the arithmetic on price lines. The installation manager types each line's scope, quantity, unit price, exclusions and validity date, and the sheet multiplies quantity by unit price. That typing is the capture, and it stays in the step, so the step remains at 75. Reading the bid, judging quality and reliability, and the price talk stay at 100. The sheet does not pick the subcontractor, and this task does not award the work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each bid uses its own layout, so the manager added the totals by hand from the pages.
tasks.enabler_now: A calculation sheet already multiplies quantity by unit price once the manager has typed those fields in the same columns.
tasks.still_hard: Quality and reliability are a judgement of this subcontractor. A low line can hide an exclusion. The talk about price stays with the manager.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which exclusion this installation cannot accept, and which subcontractor will still be here if the work fails.
tasks.altitude: Hand multiplication of typed price lines is shorter. The manager still reads every bid, still judges quality and reliability, and still chooses the subcontractor. No new decision right is gained.

reach.task: Receive a bid that is one lump sum rather than quantity and unit price
reach.learn: To leave that total as written and not force it into the columns

reach.task: Talk through a price the sheet has multiplied
reach.learn: That the line total is not an offer and the manager still decides

evidence.claim: A calculation sheet multiplies quantity by unit price after those fields are typed. It does not judge a subcontractor's quality or reliability. Model knowledge.
Annex III 4(b) makes high-risk an AI system that allocates tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or that evaluates worker performance.
Names, hours and output per worker are personnel data and performance observation, and they need works-council consent.

assumptions: The boundary is one set of subcontractor bids for one installation. The manager does not award the work in this task. Reading, the quality judgement, and the price talk stay at 100.

Comparison columns are scope line, quantity, unit price, exclusions and validity date. The producer is the installation manager, who types them from the bid in that same step. The sheet then multiplies quantity by unit price and sums the lines. A bid that is one lump sum, or that will not fit those columns, is totalled by hand inside the same step, which is why that step remains at 75 rather than lower.

The quality and reliability judgement does not read the sheet total. The discussion uses both the totals and the judgement, and it is not shortened. The sheet stores bid lines only. It does not store a named worker's hours or output, so works-council consent for that data is not triggered here.
unknowns: How often these bids arrive as quantity and unit price rather than one lump sum.
Whether an estimator, rather than the installation manager, already types the price lines today.
research_questions: Of the last ten subcontractor bids, how many had separate quantity and unit price lines a sheet can multiply, and how many were a single lump sum?

incremental.description: Typing the columns is the comparison step itself, so the manager has no extra upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Bids that arrive as one lump sum, or in a shape that will not fit the columns. The manager still types or still adds by hand, and still judges quality and reliability in full, so little of the arithmetic step goes away.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The installation manager still walks the site and still draws the piping and instrumentation architecture. A sheet shortens only the multiplication of price lines the manager has typed. The manager still judges subcontractor quality and reliability and still chooses the subcontractor. Nothing is awarded by the sheet, and no diagram is drawn from a photo.
reach: Estimator: a bid whose price is one lump sum. Learn to leave that total as written.
Subcontractor: a price talk. Learn that a multiplied line total is not an offer.
Crew lead: a route the diagram did not show. Learn to stop until the manager revises the diagram.
skills_to_grow: Reject a process flow diagram that does not match the piping and instrumentation on this site.
Reject a low bid whose exclusions this installation cannot accept.
Do not record a named worker's hours or output on the bid sheet.
role.ambitious_version: Price lines for a subcontractor bid sit in the same columns, and the sheet multiplies them. The manager still chooses the subcontractor and still draws the system architecture on the site.
